purpose: Read-only feasibility review while A0006 confirmation runs; not an attempt, benchmark or supported speedup.

sources.claim: Mapped pinned host memory can be accessed by kernels. Discrete-GPU usefulness depends on access pattern; coalesced one-time reads are the intended case.
Host memory must be mapped/page-locked and GPU access must use its device pointer where required.

local_launcher.review: getPointer queries CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_DEVICE_POINTER for objects with data_ptr(). A pinned-host tensor may be accepted if driver maps it; must test capability, not assume ordinary CPU tensor is accessible.

hypothesis: One GPU gather from mapped pinned CPU table could replace CPU lookup plus explicit H2D and potentially GPU-ID D2H staging. Table remains host-resident; reads must be fresh on every forward.
risks: PCIe read latency/bandwidth and SM occupancy can be worse than DMA-engine copies.
Entire3000MiB table becomes page-locked; host memory accounting must explicitly include it.
Keep host allocation alive until every kernel completes; close/error cleanup must synchronize before freeing.
GPU-ID and CPU-ID paths, cross-stream callers, repeated weights/IDs, exactness and bounds handling require tests.
No GPU/CPU prototype measurements were run concurrently with A0006 formal timing.
next_action: After timing is idle, separately profile small/full-row direct mapped reads against existing gather+H2D before deciding whether to register a model candidate.
